text:
Nina: Heads-up — eu-west3 GPU pool is seeing a bunch of failed allocs. Several nodes stuck in Provisioning-Wait. Kernel logs show repeated `nvme error: ctrl 0000:01:00.0 lost command`, SMART spikes. Anyone oncall?
janitor-bot: ALERT: nvme0 SMART attribute 241/5 (interface CRC) increasing on gnode-2378, flagged for scrub and quarantine.
Mike: I'm oncall. grabbing dmesg now, quick snippet: ```Mar 10 03:07:12 gnode-2378 kernel: nvme nvme0: I/O 0 QID 1 timeout, aborting
Mar 10 03:07:13 gnode-2378 kernel: nvme0n1: requeueing IO due to anonymous error status: 0x40000200
Mar 10 03:07:14 gnode-2378 kernel: nvme nvme0: reset controller (reset-type 2)```
Leo: Is this aligned with the nightly scrub window? We had a scrub cadence bump last week.
Nina: Scrub started 03:00 UTC in eu-west3 and looked normal until 03:06 when the first `device offline` showed up. Multiple nodes show transient thermal/IO spikes.
Mike: Sensors show temp jump then fan rpm dip on 2378/2381. iostat shows write queue length spike and high svctm. suspect thermal+firmware interplay.
Sara: If we quarantine too many nodes we starve GPU capacity. What's the immediate provisioning impact? How many pending GPU jobs will be delayed?
ops-oncall: I'm going to cordon impacted nodes and flip the GPU routing policy to fallback pools in us-west2 for new allocations. Will post command and status.
Mike: mitigation plan: pause janitor scrub for eu-west3 for 30m, reduce fstrim concurrency to 1, and temporarily lower scrub parallelism. Quick annotation to pause: `kubectl annotate nodes -l region=eu-west3 scrub.pause=true --overwrite` (will follow with a safer patch).
Nina: Affected nodes: gnode-2378, gnode-2381, gnode-2389, gnode-2390. Two of them already in `ReadOnly` after controller reset.
Leo: Long term we should ask HW to check for cohort firmware known issues — some controllers have epochal wear patterns that trigger CRC/timeout storms under concurrent scrub. Might need a firmware patch or per-node blacklist for bad blocks.
Sara: Cost / perf note: routing GPUs to us-west2 adds cross-region latency and increases egress/burst infra cost. Forecasted bump ~+10% for the next 2-4 hours if fallback remains. Might be cheaper than failed job retries though.
ops-oncall: Actioning now: cordon + drain (allow-running=false) on the four nodes, label `nvme-hot=true`, public status: https://r-infra/incident/1795550000 (creating ticket and paging hw-supply). ETA cordon+route: 18m.
Mike: I'll collect `iostat -x 1 10`, `smartctl -a` for each node and upload to the incident doc. Also capturing `nvme-cli` logs and kernel oops.
Nina: Thanks — ping me when nodes are cordoned. I'll coordinate with capacity-planning to temp-boost dedicated capacity if fallback pool hits >80% utilization.
Leo: For follow-up: schedule a fw/SMART sweep for the cohort, adjust scrub cadence in eu-west3 during hot hours, and add a probe to detect the temp+io pattern so janitor-bot can preemptively back off.
ops-oncall: Confirmed: cordon started, two nodes drained cleanly, two hit io error and drained into standby. Routing switched. Paging hw-supply and SRE. Will update incident timeline in 1h. :eyes:
Sara: Please include an estimate of lost GPU-hours and expected cost delta in the incident. We need that for the customer-impact call.
Mike: Uploaded logs to incident page and attached `iostat` outputs. Will run `nvme fw-log` next and check vendor flash health counters.
Nina: Good work — keep threads tight. We'll do a postmortem once hw-supply confirms firmware path or replacement plan. :thumbsup:
